title: Long-term co-culture of primary hepatocytes and GFP-HepaRG cells for investigations on Plasmodium hypnozoites
protocol: Rinse GFP-HepaRG cells in a 25 cm² flask three times with 5 mL sterile PBS.
Add 2 mL of pre-warmed 0.25% trypsin-EDTA and return the flask to the incubator for 1 to 2 minutes.
Knock the flask sharply when cells begin to detach, then add 8 mL of culture medium rapidly.
Transfer cell suspension into a 50 mL tube and centrifuge at 500 x g for 3 min at room temperature.
Remove supernatant and re-suspend cells in 3 mL of culture medium.
Count viable GFP-HepaRG cells using a haemocytometer with Trypan Blue dye exclusion method.
Adjust the cell suspension to 0.35 million viable cells per mL.
Determine the number of freshly isolated hepatocytes and their viability, which should be >80% in order to proceed.
Adjust volume of fresh hepatocyte preparation to contain 0.8 million viable cells per mL.
Use a 15 mL tube containing 10 mL of culture medium at 4°C for cryopreserved simian primary hepatocytes.
Remove a cryovial of primary hepatocytes from the liquid nitrogen tank immediately.
Place the cryovial in a water bath at 37°C until nearly thawed, with ice crystals still visible.
Wipe the tube with a tissue soaked in 70% ethanol and transfer to a biosafety hood.
Decant the hepatocytes into 10 mL of culture medium at 4°C.
Invert the tube gently 2-3 times.
Centrifuge the mixture at 200 x g for 3 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the cells in 10 mL of 40% iso-osmotic Percoll and centrifuge at 900 x g for 3 min at room temperature.
Determine cell number and viability, which should be greater than 90% to proceed.
Adjust the volume of the cell suspension to contain 0.8 million viable cells per mL.
Deposit 20 µL of HepaRG cells (7,000 cells) in the center of each well of a collagen I-coated 48-well plate.
Add 250 µL of hepatocytes (200,000 cells) to each well containing HepaRG cells.
Transfer the plate into the incubator immediately and do not disturb until cells are attached.
Replace the culture medium the next day prior to infection.
Prepare 3 Petri dishes with 8 mL of L15 medium.
Kill mosquitoes in 70% ethanol.
Rapidly wash mosquitoes in the first Petri dish.
Repeat washing by dipping mosquitoes in the second and third Petri dishes.
Align mosquitoes on a sterile glass slide under a stereomicroscope.
Under a stereomicroscope, separate mosquito heads from thoraxes using needles while pressing the thorax to extrude salivary glands.
Remove salivary glands with L15 medium to the homogenizer placed on ice.
Homogenize the salivary glands.
Filter the suspension through a 40 µm cell strainer in a 50 mL tube placed on ice.
Centrifuge to recover sporozoites at 16,000 x g for 3 minutes at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant and re-suspend the sporozoites in culture medium.
Count the number of sporozoites in a haemocytometer and adjust the concentration to 800,000 sporozoites per mL.
Keep the sporozoite suspension on ice until use.
Rinse the co-cultured cells with 300 µL of culture medium per well.
Remove the wash culture medium and replace with 125 µL of culture medium per well.
Add 125 µL of sporozoites per well (100,000 sporozoites).
Centrifuge the plate at 900 x g for 10 min at 4 °C without brake.
Carefully remove the plate from the centrifuge and return it to the incubator for 3-4 hours.
Wash the infected cells three times with 300 µL of culture medium per well.
Remove the wash culture medium before adding 300 µL of fresh culture medium per well and replace the plate in the incubator.
Change the medium every 48 hours.
Thaw Matrigel on ice.
Carefully remove the medium after the 3-4 hours of incubation.
Rinse the infected cells three times with 300 µL of culture medium per well.
Remove the wash culture medium.
Pipette 100 µL of Matrigel using a cold tip and gently overlay the cells in each well.
Return the plate to the incubator for 30 minutes to allow the Matrigel to gel.
Add 300 µL of culture medium to each well.
Replace the plate in the incubator.
Every 48 hours, carefully aspirate the medium.
Take care not to disturb the Matrigel.
Replace it with 300 µL of fresh culture medium.
At day 5 post-infection, fix 3 wells for parasite immunostaining.
Prepare sufficient atovaquone solution for 3 days of treatment.
Dilute the atovaquone in culture medium to a final concentration of 551 nM (~202.13 ng per mL).
Prepare three 400 µl aliquots (one per day) and store at 4 °C.
At days 5, 6, and 7, carefully remove the culture medium from each well.
Add 300 µL of the atovaquone in culture medium to each well.
At day 8, fix 3 treated and three untreated wells for parasite immunostaining.
Remove the medium and the Matrigel by aspiration.
Add 200 µL of 4% PFA to each well to fix the cells by incubation at RT for 15 minutes.
Rinse the wells 3 times with 300 µL of PBS.
Add 200 µL of 0.1% Triton X-100 and incubate at RT for 10 minutes.
Rinse the wells 3 times with 300 µL of PBS.
To each well, add 150 µL of mouse polyclonal serum raised against PfHSP70 at a 1/2,000 dilution or use other suitable antibodies at appropriate dilutions, or stain with Giemsa.
Incubate for 45 minutes at 37°C.
Rinse the wells 3 times with 300 µL of PBS.
To each well, add 150 µL of Alexa Fluor 488 goat anti-mouse IgG (H+L) diluted 1/600.
Incubate for 45 minutes at 37°C.
Rinse the wells 3 times with 300 µL of PBS.
Enumerate the parasites under a fluorescence microscope at a 200X magnification.
Avoid shaking co-cultured cells during handling to prevent perturbation.
Maintain constant temperature when adding medium to infected co-cultured cells.
Ensure complete removal of Matrigel for good fixation.
